question: The magnetic moment of a bar magnet is doubled while the distance of the point from the centre of the magnet remains the same. How will the magnetic field at a point on its axial line change? Justify your answer.

options.A: The axial magnetic field becomes four times because $B_{\text{axial}}\propto M^2$.
options.B: For a short bar magnet, $B_{\text{axial}}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{2M}{r^3}$, so at fixed $r$, $B_{\text{axial}}\propto M$. Doubling $M$ therefore doubles the axial magnetic field.
options.C: The axial magnetic field remains unchanged because it depends only on distance from the magnet.
options.D: The axial magnetic field becomes half because the magnetic moment is doubled.
